newsitem.title: UK: BA puts Heathrow catering business on sale.
newsitem.headline: BA puts Heathrow catering business on sale.

text.p: British Airways said on Thursday it was planning to sell its in-flight catering production operations at London's Heathrow airport.

BA said it had taken the decision after a study showed its catering department would face increasing competition from specialist catering companies which today form part of more efficient global businesses.
The airline ruled out any job losses saying the staff working at the two Heathrow bases are protected by current transfer of employment legislation.
"Discussions will now begin with potential buyers, with a view to the handover of the business in the year," BA said in a statement.

As part of the sale, BA would sell its long-haul catering operation where 1,200 British Airways employees produce about 25,000 meals a day and its short-haul catering where its contractors produce around 25,000 meals a day.

"This important supply industry is consolidating very quickly. A small number of large and efficient global catering businesses will in future compete for airline contracts," BA's chief executive Bob Ayling said.
"We will seek a purchaser who is committed to excellent employee relations, investment and improvement," he said.
The airline's catering outside London is already provided externally by about 80 specialist catering contractors who produce a total of 60,000 meals a day.
